summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with chest pain, abdominal pain, fever, and weakness, one day after symptom onset. She had recently been discharged with presumed infectious colitis and was on Augmentin for a slow-healing sternal wound from prior CABG. Initial workup revealed leukocytosis and a new right bundle branch block, but no acute ischemia. Stool testing confirmed C. difficile infection, prompting discontinuation of Augmentin and initiation of oral vancomycin and metronidazole. Her condition improved with treatment, including hydration for acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease, insulin adjustment for diabetes, and wound care with transition from wound vac to wet-to-dry dressings. She regained strength, tolerated a regular diet, and was discharged to extended care with a plan to complete a 14-day vancomycin course and continue rehabilitation for residual stroke weakness.
problems: Intestinal infection due to Clostridium difficile
Late effects of cerebrovascular disease, hemiplegia affecting unspecified side
Diabetes with renal manifestations, type II or unspecified type, uncontrolled
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease, unspecified, with chronic kidney disease stage I through stage IV, or unspecified

Surgical operation with anastomosis, bypass, or graft, with natural or artificial tissues used as implant causing abnormal patient reaction, or later complication, without mention of misadventure at time of operation
